days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday is Art Hop night, and we’re walking it together. The 34th South End Art Hop itself runs 5 to 10 across the South End, and Friday is by far the most spectacular as Pine Street closes to cars from Kilburn to Howard for the night, Local Motion runs a free bike valet at the Barge Canal at 377 Pine, and there is free parking and shuttle pickup at the Innovation Center at 128 Lakeside Ave. And if you want to go, and also wanted a crowd with you, our own South End Art Hop with BTown crew [MEETUP] meets at 6 outside the main entrance of the Soda Plant at 266 Pine Street, hangs there for a minute, then heads out at 6:15 to wander studios, galleries, pop ups and food trucks with no set route, and you can peel off whenever you like. Along Pine Street, Milton Busker & The Grim Work play a free set at the Venetian Soda Lounge at 7 and the Third Annual Rocketship Show fills Conant Metal and Light from 6 to 10 with Rusty and the Big Jump headlining. Up the street, BCA Studios opens its doors from 5 to 8 at 405 Pine for a self guided walk through the painting, print, clay and metals studios, Upstate Elevator's Lot Jam turns its lot at 699 Pine into a free block party from 5 to 10 with Clean Fill at 5:30 and Dobbs' Dead at 7, three bands play the Green Door Studio on Howard Street for free starting at 5, and Dana Mashoian Walrath's installation The Book of Genocides is on view at the Maltex Building from 5 to 9. Downtown, Justin LaPoint plays a free 4 PM set at Hotel Vermont, the Lane Series opens with jazz singer Cyrille Aimée ($5-40) at the UVM Recital Hall at 7:30, comedian Matt Mathews ($46.25-212) plays the Flynn at 7 and again at 10:15, All Your Friends , an indie sleaze dance party, opens its doors at Higher Ground at 8:30 for the 18 plus crowd, and Dennis McSorley's solo show Typhoon of Tenderness runs at Off Center at 7:30 by donation, Friday and Saturday. In South Burlington, Rhythm & Reels takes over Rick Marcotte Central School from 6 to 9:30, free, with The Night Shift playing, Yong Suk's Korean Kitchen serving and the movie Goat outdoors after the music, and up on Northgate Road, AJH Dance Aerobics & Strength opens with a free class at Northgate Community Hall from 5 to 6.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday is the full day of the Hop, and we start it with coffee. BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] takes the outdoor tables at Zero Gravity at 10, and Zero Gravity sits right in the middle of everything. Art Hop runs 10 to 10, with the Artist Market at the Dealer.com lot at Howard and Pine from 10 to 4 and Kids Hop kicking off at the Burlington Farmers Market , which runs 9 to 2 at 345 Pine with over 70 vendors. The Brain Freezer 5K starts at North Beach at 10 with a pint of ice cream waiting at the halfway point for anyone racing, and registration is $40 until 11:59 tonight, $50 after. STRUT! ($25-35) puts seven Vermont designers on the runway at the SEABA Center, 400 Pine, at 5 and 8:30 with doors a half hour before each show, Amber LeMay as MC, and the Hat Bop hatwalk opening the 5 PM show. Dancing With The Burlington Stars fills the Flynn at 7, local celebrities paired with dance professionals competing for the title, with all proceeds going to the Vermont Association for the Blind and Visually Impaired. Out in Essex Junction, Rainbow Kitten Surprise ($58.50-62.50) plays the Midway Lawn at the Champlain Valley Expo with Cigarettes @ Sunset, doors 6:30, show at 8, rain or shine, blankets and chairs welcome, no outside food or drink, and kids 12 and under get in free. Pride weekend starts early. Our Flag Means Pride is a nautical burlesque and drag variety show at the Main Street Landing Black Box, doors 7, show at 8, free with a sign up to reserve a seat. Showing Up Whole , a free aikido workshop for the LGBTQ+ community and allies, runs 1 to 2:15 at Aikido of Champlain Valley on Pine Street with registration encouraged, and Queeraoke with Lizzie Murderz keeps Standing Stone Wines in Winooski singing at 9. The fifth annual Parking Lot Dance Party at College Street Church starts with a free picnic at 4:30, a beginner swing lesson at 5:30 and the Green Mountain Swing big band from 6 to 7:30. Jesse Taylor Band and Yabai! play a free double bill in the Community Room at BCA Studios from 7 to 10, The Volcanos play Sterling Hardwoods at 9 for free, and kids can make sock puppets at King Street Laundry from 11 to 3. Big Pond Improv Festival ($5-25 a show) runs six shows at Vermont Comedy Club from noon to 9:30 with a family hour first and a $75 pass for the whole festival, Partizanfilm screens The Resurrection of Victor Jara at 6 with a filmmaker Q&A, and Dance For Freedom ($33) runs at Spiral House from 7 to 9. South Burlington runs the SB Color Run at Veterans Memorial Park with check in at 1 and the color toss at 1:30, then a free community dinner at the Senior Center on Market Street from 5:30 to 7, catered by The Dominican Spot, with advance registration required. Winooski has the Community Clean-Up Crew meeting outside Specs at 8:30 and Green Mountain Gloves amateur boxing at Combat Fitness MMA, doors at noon, bouts 1 to 4, admission by donation. Shelburne Orchards hosts Hot Pickin' Party bluegrass from 12 to 2, free, and board gamers get Board Game Brunch [MEETUP] at Old Town Cafe & Comics in Williston from 9 to 12.

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday belongs to Pride. The Pride Vermont Parade steps off downtown at noon and marches up Church and Pearl to Battery Park, where the free festival runs 1 to 4 with music, food and community booths, and the Flynn's Playing Fields sends giant inflatable sea creatures floating through the parade, free and drop in. If you want to be in it, march with Fletcher Free Library at 11, registration required and they email the meeting spot, or ride with Local Motion , staging in the Hood Plant lot at 182 King Street between 10 and 11. Art Hop closes out from 11 to 4 with artist vendors at the Dealer.com lot and a Designers and Wearables Market at 400 Pine from 11 to 3, and Brio Coffeeworks in the Soda Plant hosts a drag story hour at 10:30. Nashville's Sicard Hollow bring their bluegrass to the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge with The Tenderbellies, doors at 7, all ages. The Sunday Polo Match ($10-20) at Amdez Polo Club in Shelburne goes at 3, tailgate style, and families can catch Anna Adler singing and telling stories at Shelburne Orchards from 10 to 11 for free. Readers have the Food For Talk Cookbook Club at the library from 3 to 5 with Feast as this month's book, register first, and a pair of Front Street neighbors are hosting a plant based potluck in their garden from 4:30 to 7 for 1 Million Tables, bring a dish, RSVP optional.
